claim: ZTHR is in production use for greenfield systems in a regulated industry, where it has proven highly effective.
gap: No artifact, metric, baseline or third-party attestation in the repo. 'Highly effective' has no denominator.
proposedEvidence: Publish the six standard dimensions the paper itself names (PAPER.md:852) for at least one production application vs its incumbent process, as an anonymised, dated report signed by someone other than the author; or narrow the sentence to 'in use' with no efficacy adjective until then.

claim: Every change is reviewed by at least three model families before commit, and a fourth in place before promotion.
evidence: ref control/review.yaml (4 seats declared)
ref docs/review.md:47 ('Review by models from other families is designed and switched off')
intent/factory/review-on-vertex.patch (not applied)
intent/test/agents.test.ts 'reviews come from other families...' (requires 2, not 3)
gap: No pipeline step runs model review (ref cloudbuild.yaml has none); no recorded review verdicts exist for any commit; the intent agent API requires two families, not three plus one; the 844f589 'independent review' was same-family sessions.
proposedEvidence: Turn review on as a required Cloud Build step that writes one signed verdict record per seat per commit (model id, provider response id, diff hash, verdict). Gate: commit admitted only if >=3 distinct provider families have verdicts on its exact tree hash. Third-party check: script that walks git log and joins each commit to its verdict records; fails on any commit missing one. Until then narrow to 'designed for'.

claim: Every protected branch carries rules with no bypass actors; live rules are compared against a committed expectation; there is no path that skips admission.
evidence: GitHub API /branches/main and /branches/reference-implementation: protected=false, required_status_checks off; /rules/branches/*: [] (queried 2026-11-27)
ref control/required-checks.yaml + zero-bypass gate compares only with cloudbuild.yaml
gap: Neither main nor reference-implementation is protected and there are no rulesets; agents push straight to the deploy branch and checks run after the push. The zero-bypass gate compares a YAML list with another YAML file, not with GitHub's live rules.
proposedEvidence: Enable a ruleset on main and reference-implementation (no bypass actors, required checks = required-checks.yaml, block force-push/deletion, require PR). Add a scheduled workflow that reads GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/{b} and fails if it differs from control/branch-rules.json. Proof of bite: a planted test that feeds the comparator a ruleset missing one check and must fail. Re-runnable by anyone via the public API.

claim: AI writes the code; no human writes code.
source: SUMMARY.md:94; profile of the pipeline ('zero human code')
evidence: git log intent-surface: 90 claude-agent + 14 Claude authored, 16 'Russ Little' (all on early main: site/index.html 2,738 lines, deploy.yml, firebase.json, README)
ref branch: 146/146 commits by Claude/claude-agent
gap: Authorship is the git author string, which anyone can set. Human-authored commits exist on main (site HTML, deploy workflow). No attestation ties a commit to an agent session.
proposedEvidence: Narrow to 'every commit on reference-implementation and intent-surface after <date> is authored by an agent identity'. Make it checkable: agent commits signed by an agent-only SSH key whose public half is in control/allowed-signers; a CI check fails any commit to code paths not signed by that key or (for person-only paths) by a listed person's key; publish allowed-signers so `git log --show-signature` reproduces it.

claim: Every named safety gate is proven to fail on its planted defect, with the proof pinned to the gate's hash; editing a gate makes the proof stale and fails the build.

proposedEvidence: (1) Restore a green reference build and publish the gates step log as an artifact per commit. (2) Add to CI a meta-test: for one gate, mutate its check function (e.g. replace body with 'return pass') and assert `GATES_VERIFY=1 npm run gates` exits non-zero — proves staleness detection bites. (3) Either add tools/gates.ts to intent or remove the script and stop claiming gates for the intent line.

claim: Done means serving: deploy by content hash, rollback target captured, serving equals built, unauthorized callers refused, release record on success and failure.

Third party re-runs: compare published digest with `crane digest` of the public image tag.
